source_notes: repo https://github.com/pola-rs/polars; merged PR or fixed issue

facts.claim: Issue #22664 exists: 'scan_parquet on multiple files not parallel anymore since 1.28', opened May 8 2025 by fingoldo, closed as completed on July 3 2025

The issue has exactly one comment (June 12 2025, reporter): converting categoricals to strings in the Parquet files made the glob read parallel and fast again; reporter suspects categorical merging across files
Reported timings: about 50 s on 1.26.0 and 1.27.0; about 5 min on 1.28.0 and 1.29.0 (query over ~143 files, sort, collect; reporter on Windows, non-AVX2 CPU, polars-lts-cpu)

The issue's closing PR is #23016 'refactor: Rework Categorical/Enum to use (Frozen)Categories', merged July 3 2025; it reimplements Categorical/Enum and does not describe any change to multi-file scan parallelism or row-group scheduling
The seed's reference ('the upstream fix PR, to be identified') is a parallelism fix for multi-file scan_parquet
PR #23016 shipped in Polars 1.32.0 (released 2025-08-01 per piwheels); 1.32.0 highlights list the Categorical/Enum rework
No merged or open PR implementing parallel multi-file / glob / hive scan_parquet exists (GitHub PR search for scan_parquet parallel glob returned 0 results)
A maintainer has confirmed the root cause of the parallelism loss
Repository licence is MIT (Copyright 2025 Ritchie Vink; also NVIDIA notice for some portions)

spike_plan.kill_if: 1.28 and 1.27 medians are within 20%, or the regression does not reproduce on current head; then there is no regression to restore.
spike_plan.pass_if: Median 1.28 time is at least 3x the 1.27 time on the same data, and the string-categorical variant is fast on 1.28 (confirming a categorical-merge cause).
steps: In a networked throwaway container, pip install polars==1.27.0 and polars==1.28.0 (PyPI wheels; the spike may use network, the task may not).
Generate about 143 small parquet files with a categorical column and a timestamp, matching the issue's shape.
Time scan_parquet(glob).sort('timestamp').collect() on each version, 5 runs each; record median and CPU utilisation.
Repeat with the categorical column converted to string to confirm the reporter's workaround.
Check whether the slowdown reproduces on current py-2.0.0 head (build the wheel only if the PyPI check is ambiguous).
If the slowdown reproduces, bisect the categorical path only to confirm cause; do not start the full build.

v1.summary: The seed's premise holds in part: issue #22664 reports a real multi-file scan_parquet slowdown from 1.27 to 1.28 with a string-categorical workaround, under MIT. But the closing PR #23016 is a categorical rework that does not address parallelism, so the claimed reference and the base-with-regression are not established. Killed as K5 pending a spike that reproduces the slowdown and identifies a fix.
